title: BCMA relapse
subtitle: One patient, longitudinal evidence, antigen-loss routing
hypothesis: Why did this patient relapse after an initial response and fail retreatment with the same CAR-T product? Rank competing mechanisms, link each claim to measured evidence, and propose a discriminating next experiment.
description: A real prepared Brev packet that tests identity correction, post-treatment timing and the boundary between truncating variants and binder redesign.

evidence.title: One patient; eight longitudinal samples
evidence.summary: The prepared case describes one patient and eight longitudinal bone-marrow RNA samples. The baseline was depleted of CD138-positive cells and is not an unbiased baseline tumor sample.

values.baseline_note: CD138-positive cells depleted; not an unbiased pretreatment tumor sample

evidence.title: Corrected S5/S6 sample identities
evidence.summary: The prepared manifest maps sample_05/GSM5013825 to matrix S6 and metadata S5, and sample_06/GSM5013826 to matrix S5 and metadata S6. These mapped samples must not be interchanged by filename.

source.name: sample_manifest.tsv
source.locator: Rows where alias_disagreement=True; sample_05 and sample_06

values.qualification: Prepared-manifest measurements retained; large H5 objects not reprocessed in the demo.

evidence.title: Post-treatment TNFRSF17 truncating variant
evidence.summary: The post-second-infusion source table reports TNFRSF17 p.Q38* (Nonsense_Mutation), PASS, tumor alternate count 10 of depth 41. This is post-treatment evidence and does not establish when the alteration arose or biallelic loss by itself.

evidence.title: Copy number and surface protein remain unresolved here
evidence.summary: The prepared case explicitly requires qualified copy-number inference and warns that RNA non-detection is not surface-protein measurement. A truncating variant plus this metadata does not establish an exclusive resistance mechanism.

limitations: Count one patient, not eight patients or thousands of independent clinical replicates.
Do not infer loss of tumor expression by comparing an unbiased tumor sample with the CD138-depleted baseline.
Use sample_manifest.tsv for sample identity; source S5/S6 names disagree across files and have been reconciled by all retained barcodes.
Post-treatment variant presence does not establish that it was absent before treatment.
The allele-count table is input to copy-number inference, not a table of final copy-number calls. File1/File2 orientation and analysis parameters must be established before running that inference.
All-cell pseudobulk mixes changing cell populations; analyze appropriate cell types before mechanistic interpretation.
RNA non-detection is not a surface-protein measurement.
Report contradictions and unmeasured alternatives, and distinguish a supported explanation from exclusive causal proof.
Only compact case metadata, sample manifest and mutation table are bundled; H5, cell metadata and allele-count matrices remain on Brev.
This is open-book development, not a blinded evaluation against the published mechanism.

demo_decision.summary: A post-treatment TNFRSF17 truncating variant makes antigen escape plausible, but this compact packet cannot establish biallelic loss, its timing, or exclusive causality. Qualify target presence before proposing a same-target design.

next_experiment.title: Resolve accessible BCMA and allelic context
next_experiment.design: Validate tumor-cell identity, surface-accessible BCMA and allele/copy-number state at matched timepoints; interpret CAR-T activity with target-present and target-absent controls.
next_experiment.positive: Concordant loss of accessible BCMA with qualified allelic evidence supports an antigen-selection or multi-target research objective.
next_experiment.negative: Retained accessible BCMA weakens a complete target-loss explanation and shifts attention to functional alternatives.
next_experiment.inconclusive: RNA-only evidence, uncertain cell identity or unqualified allele-count orientation cannot establish functional antigen loss.

rd_handoff.objective: Establish functional target availability, then select an antigen-selection or qualified retained-target design objective.
rd_handoff.reference: Original ide-cel target is BCMA; no exact reference/candidate construct is bundled.

candidates.name: BCMA target-retention assay
candidates.rationale: Measure surface-accessible BCMA in correctly identified tumor samples; retain sample timing and required allelic evidence before selecting a design branch.
candidates.endpoint: Surface-accessible BCMA recognition; specify sample, infusion-relative timing, units and controls.
candidates.exact_sequences: Not supplied. This is a planned assay arm, not a qualified or modeled molecular construct.

modeling.reason: Observed p.Q38* is truncating. No missense comparison or supported affinity rescue can be inferred; a target-retained binder comparison requires a separately qualified construct packet.

return_requirements: Sample/experiment IDs and timing relative to the correct infusion
Tumor-cell identity and corrected manifest mapping
Surface recognition and copy-number/allelic artifacts with QC
Independent replicate definition, units and controls
